question: Can a larger universal G transfer across galaxies and cluster lensing when completion is a bounded tensor whose projection depends on the local tidal eigendirections?

root_equation.solar_limit: large tidal norm implies A_T -> 0, C_ij -> C_solar delta_ij, and g -> gbar
root_equation.maximum_limit: all eigenvalues of P lie in [0,1], so no eigenvalue of C exceeds one

sample.bridge: 44 MaNGA BCG points plus 72 density-resolved CLASH radial points
sample.bridge_objective: equal-domain mean of equal-system mean squared log residual
sample.SPARC: 131 galaxies; nuisances fit on 2066 inner points and tested on 968 untouched outer points
sample.raw_lensing: RX J2129 15 training and 7 already-spent heldout image positions
sample.tensor_reconstruction: spherical Poisson closure for bridge; axisymmetric Poisson closure for SPARC; resolved spherical derivative for RX J2129

selection.rule: lowest five-fold heldout bridge equal-domain RMSE; SPARC and raw images remain unseen during selection

claim_limits: This is a weak-field constitutive tensor, not a derived covariant action.
The tidal tensor is reconstructed from the available symmetry and density data rather than measured as a full three-dimensional tensor.
SPARC vertical curvature depends on a frozen primary scale-height model and must pass geometry sensitivity checks if the primary transfer succeeds.
RX J2129 uses a spherical tensor reconstruction before the existing pseudo-elliptical lens projection; it is not yet a full three-dimensional ray-traced tensor lens.
RX J2129 coordinates are an already-inspected diagnostic, not an independent holdout.
